exemplars.title: Wisdom of the Crowd, Without the Crowd: A Socratic LLM for Asynchronous Deliberation on Perspectivist Data
exemplars.why: The clearest structural match: an established crowd-deliberation procedure remains intact while one person participates asynchronously and the LLM explicitly takes the place of the other crowdworkers.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 5603 because its evidence explicitly identifies both the displaced human counterparts and their model replacement, rather than only claiming that agents emulate collaborative dynamics.

exemplars.title: TutorUp: What If Your Students Were Simulated? Training Tutors to Address Engagement Challenges in Online Learning
exemplars.why: TutorUp converts tutor–student practice into a solo training loop by assigning the student role to GPT-4o, including recognizable engagement-challenge scenarios that preserve the interpersonal procedure's purpose.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 16983 because the evidence specifies what the simulated counterpart does—conducts student conversations around engagement scenarios—whereas PairBuddy's excerpt only labels the agent an interactive partner.

exemplars.title: Beyond the Dialogue: Multi-chatbot Group Motivational Interviewing for Premenstrual Syndrome (PMS) Management
exemplars.why: This is the strongest n>2 example: it transplants the social form of group motivational interviewing into an experience where multiple chatbots fill the surrounding group roles for one participant.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: Chosen over rid 5603 because it identifies a particular established multi-party procedure and visibly retains its plurality of counterpart roles, while rid 5603 describes peer collaboration only in general terms.

notes: I retained consensus ranks 1 and 2 but replaced rank 3 (rid 5603) with rank 7 (rid 3544). Rid 5603 matches the theme, but its quote does not expose a concrete role-to-behavior mapping or name the collaborative procedure being preserved; rid 3544 more clearly transplants an established group procedure and demonstrates that the pattern extends beyond dyads. PairBuddy (rid 16983) was the closest exclusion and is structurally sound, but its supplied evidence is less operationally specific. Readers should distrust any implication that these excerpts establish detailed UI mechanics or measured effectiveness: the evidence supports role substitution, but mostly not screen-level interaction, synchronization details, or outcomes. No score was adjusted by more than 0.3.
